title: Sandiganbayan denies Marcoleta's bid for bail
summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has denied the petition for bail of Senator Rodante Marcoleta and three others who are facing a P75 million plunder charge over undeclared campaign contributions to…

blocks.text: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has denied the petition for bail of Senator Rodante Marcoleta and three others who are facing a P75 million plunder charge over undeclared campaign contributions to the lawmaker.
This was confirmed by Atty. Dennis Pulma, Clerk of Court of the Sandiganbayan Third Division.
Marcoleta’s other co-accused in the case, who will also remain in detention, are former Anakalusugan party-list Rep. Mike Defensor, businessman Joseph Espiritu, and Aristotle Viray.

Based on the criminal information filed by the Ombudsman prosecutors, the donor’s tax for the said P75 million campaign donation was only paid in December 2025, an indication of concealment since the donation was already made in January 2025.

Marcoleta, in a television interview in November 2025, said that he received P75 million donation from his friends but he did not declare this as campaign expenditure because it was upon the request of the donors to become anonymous.
The senator, however, said in his position paper submitted to the Commission on Elections (Comelec) that such donation was a personal fund of his, prompting the Comelec to stop the investigation.
This difference in Marcoleta’s accounts was included in the basis of the Ombudsman’s probe and the eventual filing of charges against Marcoleta and his co-accused. –NB, GMA News
